record.title: Event replay keys cross Project boundaries
record.description: A plugin Credential holder confined to one Project controls its Event IDs. If it knows or predicts an ID used by a different granted Project, it can submit an otherwise valid warning Event with that ID first. The shared consumer subsequently acknowledges the other Project's Event as already completed without dispatching its detection. A warning Event whose type does not produce detections can seed this state without a model call. Publisher msgID uses the same unscoped ID in the all-Project stream, creating a second place where the collision may suppress delivery. The claimed result is suppression of a target Project's observation; target-ID knowledge and a shared stream/consumer are explicit prerequisites.
record.claimed_root_cause: Project authority is present in the subject and body but omitted from replay identity: createNatsPublisher sends msgID=prepared.id and processQueued checks/marks a single shared Set using envelope.id. The API preserves producer-chosen IDs and does not establish global uniqueness. A 100000-entry size bound limits retained keys but does not isolate them.

trace.description: The producer supplies any nonempty string as its Event ID; the contract adds no Project namespace or globally unique server ID.
Scope, Project and service binding are enforced, then the original Event ID is preserved through preparation and publication.
Every Project uses prepared.id alone as the broker msgID, while the subject includes its Project.
The one stream spans all Project subjects and declares a 120-second duplicate window.
Both dummy Projects can legitimately pass the granted set; their distinct subjects and bodies pass exact reconstruction.
After the first Project's successful processing marks the ID at line 113, an Event with the same ID from the second Project is acknowledged and returned without calling process.

evidence.description: The completed-ID Set has one global string namespace and only an oldest-entry size eviction.
One deduplicator is created for the consumer serving every granted Project.
An accepted envelope type with no watcher outcomes still finishes observation processing, allowing the transport to mark its ID completed.
The watcher uses [projectId,id] for replay identity, demonstrating the stronger downstream namespace that the consumer bypasses.
Size, schema, exact subject equality and granted-Project controls are present; none changes the unscoped replay key after both valid Projects pass.

blockers: No bounded in-memory producer/consumer observation was performed: complete memory and cumulative disk sandbox controls are not established, and the assignment forbids target-code execution.
The publisher-side stream-wide msgID collision still needs a bounded observation against the pinned NATS version; no broker, deployed endpoint or external service was contacted.

Whether a single daemon consumer grants more than one Project, and whether a co-tenant plugin Credential holder can know or predict another Project's producer-chosen Event ID, are deployment and producer facts not established in source.

validation_plan.local: In a parent-approved sandbox, createEventsConsumer with a fake transport whose grantedProjectIds is ['101','202'] and emit two QueuedEvents whose subjects equal publishSubject(envelope) for valid warning envelopes with projectId 101 and 202 and the same id 'shared-event'; use a no-detection type for the first and a detection-producing type such as runtime.oom for the second. Record process calls, ackAck and nak outcomes, and stop after checking that the second Project receives no process call and is acknowledged. Independently inspect publisher options for distinct Project IDs, then use a bounded isolated broker fixture to establish msgID behavior. A regression should allow one dispatch per [Project, Event ID] while still deduplicating a replay within the same Project.
validation_plan.deployment: The owner can inspect effective stream and durable-consumer sharing, boot projectIds, and producer ID-generation rules to establish whether one consumer serves multiple Projects and whether a co-tenant could know or predict a target ID. This requires configuration and producer-source inspection, without sending live test Events.
